merger_name: Wittington Investments & Fairfax Financial – Boots Group

anzsic_codes.name: Pharmaceutical, Cosmetic and Toiletry Goods Retailing

merger_description:
Oak UK Bidco Limited (**Acquirer**) proposes to acquire the entire issued share capital of Blazing Star Boots Superco (Jersey) Limited (**Boots**) from The Boots Group Limited (**Vendor**) (the **Acquisition**).  

  

Prior to the Acquisition completing, Boots will be subject to a reorganisation with the effect that the Vendor will retain part of the Boots business that operates in Mexico and Germany.  

  

On completion of the Acquisition, the Acquirer, which is a special purpose vehicle, will be jointly owned and controlled by Wittington Investments, Limited (**Wittington Investments**) and Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited (**Fairfax**).  

  

Wittington Investments is the private holding company for the Weston family based in Canada. Wittington invests globally through a diversified portfolio of direct and fund investments.  

  

Fairfax Financial is a financial holding company based in Toronto, Canada. Through its portfolio companies, Fairfax focuses mainly on property and casualty insurance, reinsurance and the associated investment management.  

  

Boots, and its associated business lines, is a health and beauty retail business with its main office in London and its headquarters in Nottingham, United Kingdom. Boots serves customers and patients through a combination of owned businesses, equity method investments and franchise-owned locations across a diverse range of markets.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information, the ACCC considers that the Acquisition is
unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of competition given
there is no horizontal overlap or vertical relationship between Boots
and Oak BidCo, Wittington Investments or Fairfax Financial (or their
connected entities) in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
